'''''Weird West''''' is an [[action role-playing]] [[video game]] developed by [[WolfEye Studios]] and published by [[Devolver Digital]]. The game was released for [[Windows]], [[PlayStation 4]] and [[Xbox One]] on March 31, 2022, and for [[PlayStation 5]] and [[Xbox Series X/S]] subtitled ''Definitive Edition'' on May 8, 2023.

==Gameplay==
''Weird West'' is a top-down [[action role-playing game]] with elements of the [[immersive sim]] genre, with randomized elements through each playthrough. The game is based on the [[Weird West]] genre it borrows its title from, and is set in an [[open world]] environment based on the [[American frontier]].<ref name="WW">{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-12-13-weird-west-is-a-gun-slinging-fantasy-action-rpg-from-former-dishonored-prey-devs |title='Weird West' is a gun-slinging fantasy action-RPG from former Dishonored, Prey devs |first=Matt |last=Wales |date=December 13, 2019 |accessdate=February 4, 2020 |work=[[Eurogamer]] |publisher=Gamer Network}}</ref> The game features the stories of five unique characters, such as the retired bounty hunter who is forced to pick up her iron again, the pigman whose human brain was put into a body of stitched pig parts, and a Native American hunter (based on the [[Anishinaabe]] peoples). Each of the characters have their own background and story that their main quests will point to. Finishing one character's chapter will proceed the player to the next character, where the player can also find and recruit previous characters the player has played as. The world is designed to be interactive and responsive to the player's action. For instance, when the player shoots at an ammo box, it will explode.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.playstation.com/2021/07/15/weird-west-comes-to-ps4-this-fall/|title=Weird West comes to PS4 this fall|first=Raphaël|last=Colantonio|work=[[PlayStation Blog]]|date=July 15, 2021|accessdate=October 30, 2021}}</ref> Actions done by the player in the game are permanent, meaning that they cannot be undone through [[respawning]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/weird-west-dishonored-wolfeye-colantonio-interview-180055798.html|title=Respawns won't save you in 'Weird West'|first=Jessica|last=Conditt|work=[[Engadget]]|date=July 17, 2020|accessdate=October 30, 2021}}</ref> The game also features a [[permadeath]] mode in which the player character and their companions will die permanently. Actual gameplay is similar to that of a [[twin-stick shooter]], with the team describing it as "action-y version of ''[[Fallout (video game)|Fallout 1]]'' or ''[[Fallout 2|2]]''".<ref name="USG interview">{{cite web |last=Olsen |first=Matthew |date=July 16, 2020 |title=Weird West: Making an Immersive Sim From With a Distributed Team, and Without Chris Avellone |url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/weird-west-interview-raphael-colantonio-wolfeye-immersive-sim |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200718134706/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/weird-west-interview-raphael-colantonio-wolfeye-immersive-sim |archive-date=July 18, 2020 |accessdate=October 30, 2021 |work=[[USgamer]]}}</ref>

== Development ==
[[Raphaël Colantonio]] and Julien Roby, Arkane Studios' former Executive Producer, announced in November 2019 they had earlier formed a new studio, WolfEye Studios, a twenty-person studio working distributively.<ref name="Colantonio">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2019-11-20-arkane-veterans-launch-wolfeye-a-small-studio-making-big-games |title=Arkane veterans launch WolfEye: a small studio making big games |first=Rebekah |last=Valentine |work=[[GamesIndustry.biz]] |publisher=[[Gamer Network]] |date=November 20, 2019 |accessdate=February 4, 2020}}</ref> They announced their first game, ''Weird West'', at [[The Game Awards 2019]], to be published by [[Devolver Digital]]. While the game features supernatural elements, it was not designed to be a horror game. Unlike most immersive sims, the game was not played from a [[first-person perspective]], and instead adopted a [[top-down perspective]] that was inspired by the early ''[[Ultima (series)|Ultima]]'' and ''[[Fallout (franchise)|Fallout]]'' games. [[Chris Avellone]] was originally involved as a coach to the game's writing team. Since the game includes the presence of [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native Americans]], the team invited the [[Anishinaabe]] to ensure that their depiction in the game is authentic, and added [[Elizabeth LaPensée]], who is Anishinaabe and Métis, to the game's writing team.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/weird-west-developer-wolfeye-is-putting-player-agency-at-the-center-of-its-dark-immersive-sim/|title=Weird West Developer WolfEye Is Putting Player Agency at the Center of Its Dark Immersive Sim|first=Damien|last=Lawardorn|work=[[The Escapist (magazine)|The Escapist]]|date=July 30, 2021|accessdate=October 30, 2021}}</ref> Weird Wolves, a [[musical band]] established by Colantonio and Ava Gore, composed some of the game's soundtracks.<ref name="USG interview"/>  The game was released on March 31, 2022 for [[Windows]], [[PlayStation 4]], and [[Xbox One]].<ref>{{cite web|last=|first=|date=December 22, 2021|title=Weird West - A Little Longer Road: Developer Update Video|url=https://www.ign.com/videos/weird-west-a-little-longer-road-developer-update-video|work=[[IGN]]|accessdate=December 22, 2021}}</ref>

== Cultural representation ==
''Weird West'' includes a [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] [[Player character|playable character]], Across Rivers, whose storyline centers on supernatural conflict, community responsibility, and the defense of [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] people against outside threats.<ref name=":0" /> The game’s version of the [[American frontier]] draws on [[dark fantasy]] and [[Western (genre)|Western genre]] elements,<ref name="WW" /> and it also seeks to include [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] characters as part of the world’s social and cultural environment rather than leaving them out of the setting. Across Rivers’ chapter places [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] identity at the core of the game, making [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Indigenous]] representation part of the central narrative rather than just background detail.<ref name=":0" />

During development, [[Raphaël Colantonio|WolfEye Studios]] brought [[Elizabeth LaPensée]] onto the writing team.<ref name=":0" /> [[Elizabeth LaPensée|LaPensée]] is an [[Anishinaabe]] and [[Métis]] game designer, writer, artist, and researcher whose work focuses on [[Indigenous media|Indigenous-led media]], including games and comics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elizabeth LaPensée |url=https://aiis.msu.edu/people/faculty-and-staff/elizabeth-lapensee-2/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=American Indian and Indigenous Studies |language=en-US}}</ref> In interviews, [[Elizabeth LaPensée|LaPensée]] has described her work as focused on [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Indigenous]] [[self-determination]] in media and has discussed the importance of [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] creators being able to represent culture through their own creative choices rather than serving only as consultants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Magazine |first=A. MAZE |date=2020-04-29 |title=Elizabeth LaPensée |url=http://www.amaze-magazine.de/interviews/elizabeth-lapensee |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=A MAZE. Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> This is relevant to ''Weird West'' because the game includes [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] American themes in a genre that has historically relied on [[Stereotype|stereotypes]] or erased [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] perspectives.

The game’s use of the [[Western (genre)|Western genre]] also makes its representation culturally significant. Western stories commonly focus on settlers, outlaws, lawmen, and [[American frontier|frontier expansion]], while [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] peoples are often reduced to simplified roles. ''Weird West'' complicates that pattern by making a [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] character one of the game’s five main [[Protagonist|protagonists]].<ref name=":0" /> However, reviewers also noted that the game’s attempt to reimagine minorities in the historical West raised questions about how successfully it handled [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] and [[First Nations in Canada|First Nations]] culture, especially because Western [[fiction]] regularly carries a “white gaze.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ong |first=Alexis |date=March 31, 2022 |title=Weird West Review |url=https://www.thesixthaxis.com/2022/03/31/weird-west-review/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Because of this, the game can be discussed as both an example of increased [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Indigenous]] visibility in [[Video game|video games]] and as part of a broader conversation about how [[Native Americans in the United States|Native]] culture is represented in popular media.

''Weird West'' received "generally positive" reviews for PC and Xbox One<ref name="MCPC" /><ref name="MCXONE" /> and "mixed or average" reviews for PlayStation 4, according to review aggregator [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCPS4" />

''[[Destructoid]]'' liked the game's compelling story, world, exploration, frantic combat, and player choice, but lamented the presence of technical issues.<ref name="Destruct"/> ''[[Game Informer]]'' gave the game an 8.5 out of 10, writing, "''Weird West''{{'}}s best assets are its well-developed characters and deep gameplay systems, but its overall production value is underwhelming."<ref name="GI"/> ''[[GameSpot]]'' reviewed the title less positively, commending its writing, character dynamics, and old-school pulp fiction aesthetic, while taking issue with its inelegant combat, binary morality system, camerawork, unbalanced upgrade system, and stingy progression.<ref name="GSpot"/> ''[[GamesRadar+]]'' similarly praised the setting and the player's freedom to create their own story while citing the finicky morality system as problematic.<ref name="GRadar"/> ''[[IGN]]'' praised the game's bizarre encounters, twists, reveals, and chaotic stealth and combat, while criticizing the dull loot and technical issues.<ref name="IGN"/> ''[[PC Gamer]]'' praised the game's ability to react to the player's choices, but criticized its combat, writing, "When fighting does break out, it's refreshingly and mercifully quick. However, between that dingy visual style, and an overly complex twin-stick control scheme, I never found it all that enjoyable."<ref name="PCGUS"/>

During the [[26th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards]], the [[Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences]] nominated ''Weird West'' for "[[D.I.C.E. Award for Role-Playing Game of the Year|Role-Playing Game of the Year]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.interactive.org/awards/award_category_details.asp?idAward=2023&idGameAwardType=123 |title=2023 Awards Category Details Role-Playing Game of the Year |publisher=[[Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences]] |website=interactive.org |access-date=December 4, 2023}}</ref>
